s1.syndrome_frame: Acute painful vision loss with floaters and retinal detachment
salient_findings: Painful vision loss in one eye
Vitreous cells and rare anterior chamber cells
key_facts: 71-year-old woman
1-week history of symptoms
No history of myopia, ocular trauma, or surgery
Visual acuity 20/30–2 in the right eye and 20/80 in the left eye
Intraocular pressure 21 mm Hg OD and 17 mm Hg OS
Mild nuclear sclerotic cataract in the right eye
Rare anterior chamber cells and 1+ vitreous cells in the left eye
Choroidal detachments in the nasal and temporal periphery of the left eye
Overlying retinal detachment with shifting subretinal fluid in the left eye
No retinal breaks identified
Normal laboratory studies
Mild posterior scleral enhancement on MRI
Late leakage in the temporal periphery on fluorescein angiography
Shallow subretinal fluid and posterior vitreous detachment on optical coherence tomography

shortlist.label: Posterior Scleritis
shortlist.why_kept: Mild posterior scleral enhancement on MRI and clinical presentation of painful vision loss with choroidal detachments

shortlist.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of choroidal detachments, retinal detachment, and vitreous cells, which are characteristic of this disease

shortlist.label: Uveitis
shortlist.why_kept: Rare anterior chamber cells and 1+ vitreous cells, which are indicative of intraocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Central Serous Chorioretinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of shallow subretinal fluid and posterior vitreous detachment on optical coherence tomography

shortlist.label: Serous Retinal Detachment
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of retinal detachment with shifting subretinal fluid and absence of retinal breaks

raw.rationale: The presence of choroidal detachments, rare anterior chamber cells, and 1+ vitreous cells, along with mild posterior scleral enhancement on MRI, supports the diagnosis of posterior scleritis, which is an inflammation of the sclera that can lead to secondary serous retinal detachment.

rejected.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada Disease
rejected.why: Normal laboratory studies, including a normal ANCA panel, and the lack of systemic symptoms or other ocular findings typical of VKH make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Uveitis
rejected.why: While uveitis could explain some of the findings, the specific pattern of choroidal detachments and the presence of posterior scleral enhancement on MRI are more suggestive of posterior scleritis.

rejected.label: Central Serous Chorioretinopathy
rejected.why: The presence of shifting subretinal fluid and the lack of a typical 'smokestack' sign on fluorescein angiography, along with the patient's age and the involvement of the peripheral retina, make CSC less likely.

rejected.label: Serous Retinal Detachment
rejected.why: While the patient does have a serous retinal detachment, this is more of a descriptive term for the finding rather than a diagnosis; posterior scleritis provides a more specific explanation for the underlying cause of the detachment.
